trigger: Asked for ALL results of grouping an expression in every possible way, not just one best value.
key_idea: Every operator can be the last one applied; split the string there, solve both halves recursively, and combine every left result with every right result.
approach: Scan the expression for each operator position
Recursively compute all results of the left substring
Recursively compute all results of the right substring
Combine each left value with each right value using that operator
If no operator found, the substring is a single number; return it
Memoize by (left, right) to avoid recomputing substrings
gotcha: Forgetting the base case for a substring with no operator, or parsing multi-digit numbers one character at a time.

trigger: Two strings must contain exactly the same letters with the same multiplicities.
key_idea: Anagrams have identical character counts; one map that increments for s and decrements for t must end all zeros.
approach: Return false immediately if lengths differ
Walk both strings together: +1 for s[i], -1 for t[i]
Check every count in the map is zero
Return true if all zero
gotcha: Skipping the length check lets a prefix of t match s; also sorting works but costs O(n log n).

trigger: Need the minimum index gap between occurrences of two specific values in a single list.
key_idea: One pass tracking the latest index of each word; each time either updates, the current gap is a candidate minimum.
approach: Keep last seen index for word1 and word2, initialized to -1
Iterate with enumerate, update whichever word matches
Once both seen, update answer with abs(pos1 - pos2)
Return the minimum found
gotcha: Only update the minimum after both positions are set, and use the most recent occurrence of each word, not the first.

trigger: Given intervals, decide whether any two overlap.
key_idea: After sorting by start, overlaps can only happen between adjacent intervals, so compare each start with the previous end.
approach: Sort intervals by start time
Loop from index 1
If start of current < end of previous, return false
Return true after the loop
gotcha: Touching intervals (end == next start) do NOT overlap, so use strict < not <=.

trigger: Given intervals, decide whether any two overlap.
key_idea: After sorting by start, overlaps can only happen between adjacent intervals, so compare each start with the previous end.
approach: Sort intervals by start time
Loop from index 1
If intervals[i][0] < intervals[i-1][1], return false
Return true after the loop
gotcha: Touching intervals (end == next start) do NOT overlap, so use strict < not <=.

trigger: Minimum number of resources needed so that overlapping intervals never share one.
key_idea: Sort by start and keep a min-heap of end times of rooms in use; if the earliest-ending room is free before the next meeting starts, reuse it, else open a new room.
approach: Sort intervals by start
Push the first meeting's end time onto a min-heap
For each next meeting, pop the heap top if it ended at or before this start
Push this meeting's end time
Answer is the heap size at the end
gotcha: Pop at most one room per meeting (only one meeting is being seated) and use >= so back-to-back meetings share a room.

trigger: Enumerate all multisets of factors whose product is n, with no duplicate orderings.
key_idea: Choose factors in non-decreasing order starting from the last factor used, only trying divisors up to sqrt(remaining); the remaining quotient closes each combination.
approach: DFS with (min factor, remaining value, path)
If path is non-empty, record path + [remaining]
Try i from min factor to sqrt(remaining)
If i divides remaining, recurse with (i, remaining // i, path + [i])
Start from dfs(2, n, [])
gotcha: Do not record [n] alone (factors must be in [2, n-1]); starting the loop at the previous factor prevents duplicates like [2,4] and [4,2].

trigger: A list is claimed to be sorted under an unknown ordering and you must recover that ordering or detect it is impossible.
key_idea: Each adjacent word pair yields one edge from the first differing letters; Kahn's BFS topological sort produces an order, and leftover nodes mean a cycle.
approach: Initialize in-degree 0 for every letter in every word
For each adjacent pair, find first differing chars and add edge c1 -> c2 once
If no difference and the first word is longer, return empty string
Queue all letters with in-degree 0
Pop, append to result, decrement children, enqueue those hitting 0
Return result only if its length equals the letter count
gotcha: The prefix case ("abc" before "ab") is invalid, and duplicate edges must not double-count in-degree.

trigger: n+1 numbers in range [1, n] with exactly one repeated value, and constant extra space is demanded.
key_idea: Treat i -> nums[i] as a linked list; the duplicate is the entry to a cycle, found with Floyd's fast/slow pointers. The learner's cyclic-sort swap variant works but mutates the array, which the problem forbids.
approach: Set slow = fast = nums[0]
Advance slow by one step and fast by two until they meet
Reset slow to nums[0], advance both one step at a time
The meeting point is the duplicate
gotcha: Cyclic sort or marking negatives modifies nums, which violates the constraint; Floyd's cycle detection is the intended O(1) solution.

trigger: Repeatedly insert numbers and query the median of everything seen so far.
key_idea: A max-heap for the lower half and a min-heap for the upper half keep the median at the heap tops; rebalance so sizes differ by at most one.
approach: Push num to max-heap if it is <= max-heap top, else to min-heap
If max-heap has two more than min-heap, move its top over
If min-heap is larger, move its top to max-heap
Median: max-heap top if sizes differ, else average of both tops
gotcha: Python only has a min-heap, so negate values for the max-heap and remember to un-negate when reading.

trigger: Find the center node(s) of an undirected tree that minimize height when used as root.
key_idea: Peel leaves layer by layer like an onion; the last one or two nodes remaining are the centroids and the answer.
approach: Build adjacency sets; if n <= 2 return all nodes
Queue every node with degree 1
Remove a full layer of leaves, deleting them from neighbors
Add neighbors that become degree 1
Stop when at most 2 nodes remain and return them
gotcha: Handle n == 1 (no edges) up front, and process leaves layer by layer rather than one at a time, or you may strip past the center.

trigger: Keep one copy of each character while making the result lexicographically smallest.
key_idea: Build the answer on a stack; pop a larger top only if that character appears again later, so removing it now is safe.
approach: Record the last index of each character
Iterate characters; skip ones already in the result set
While top > current and top occurs later, pop it and unmark it
Push current and mark as seen
Join the stack
gotcha: Skipping already-seen characters is essential; without the seen set you would push duplicates that pops later cannot fix.

trigger: Longest contiguous subarray with an exact sum, and the array may contain negatives so sliding window fails.
key_idea: Subarray (i, r] sums to k when prefix[r] - prefix[i] == k; storing the FIRST index of each prefix sum maximizes r - i.
approach: Running total starts at 0; map prefix sum to earliest index
For each r, add nums[r] to the total
If total == k, answer is r + 1
If total - k in map, update answer with r - map[total - k]
Store total in map only if not already present
gotcha: Overwriting an existing prefix index shrinks the window; keep the earliest index (or seed map[0] = -1).

trigger: Longest substring under a constraint on the number of distinct characters.
key_idea: Expand the right end and shrink from the left while the window has more than k distinct characters; map size is the distinct count.
approach: Keep a char frequency map and left pointer
Add s[r] to the map
While map has more than k keys, decrement s[l], delete zeros, advance l
Update answer with r - l + 1
gotcha: Forgetting to delete keys whose count hits zero makes len(freq) overcount distinct characters.

trigger: Reverse an array in place with O(1) extra memory.
key_idea: Swap symmetric elements from both ends, moving pointers inward until they cross.
approach: Set l = 0 and r = len - 1
While l < r, swap s[l] and s[r]
Increment l, decrement r
gotcha: Using s = s[::-1] rebinds a new list and does not modify the caller's array; use s[:] = s[::-1] or swapping.

trigger: Reverse only elements matching a condition while leaving others in place.
key_idea: Two pointers skip non-vowels from each side, then swap the vowels they land on.
approach: Convert to a list; set first = 0, last = len - 1
Advance first until it hits a vowel
Retreat last until it hits a vowel
Swap and move both inward
Join and return
gotcha: Include uppercase vowels, and guard the inner skip loops with first < last to avoid crossing.

trigger: Return the k most frequent items from a collection.
key_idea: Count frequencies, then either keep a size-k min-heap of (count, value) or bucket values by count (max count is n) and read buckets from high to low.
approach: Count occurrences with a Counter
Create buckets indexed 0..n; put each value in bucket[count]
Walk buckets from n down to 1
Append values until k collected
gotcha: Buckets need n + 1 slots because a value can appear n times; with the heap variant pop when size exceeds k to keep the top k.

trigger: Rearrange items so identical ones are at least k positions apart, or report impossible.
key_idea: Always place the most frequent available character, then park it in a cooldown queue of length k before it becomes available again.
approach: If k == 0 return s; build a max-heap of (-count, char)
Pop the most frequent char, append it, decrement count
Push (count, char) into a waiting deque
When deque length reaches k, pop its front and re-add to heap if count > 0
Return result only if its length equals len(s)
gotcha: Re-adding a character immediately (without the k-length cooldown) breaks the distance rule; also the heap empties early when impossible, so compare lengths.

trigger: k smallest combinations across two sorted arrays.
key_idea: Each nums1[i] paired with nums2 forms a sorted list; seed a min-heap with the first pair of each row and advance j only for the row you pop.
approach: Push (nums1[i] + nums2[0], i, 0) for the first min(k, len(nums1)) rows
Pop the smallest sum and record its pair
Push (nums1[i] + nums2[j+1], i, j+1) if j+1 exists
Stop when k pairs collected or heap empty
gotcha: Seeding only min(k, len) rows keeps the heap small; pushing both (i+1, j) and (i, j+1) would create duplicates without a visited set.

trigger: kth smallest across rows that are each sorted, with memory better than O(n^2).
key_idea: Treat each row as a sorted list and merge with a min-heap of row heads; the kth pop is the answer. Binary search on value with a count-less-or-equal pass gives O(1) space.
approach: Push (matrix[r][0], r, 0) for every row
Pop k - 1 times, each time pushing the next element of that row
The next pop is the kth smallest
gotcha: Seed only min(n, k) rows and check col + 1 < n before pushing, or you index out of bounds on the last column.

trigger: Can one string be built from the letters of another, each used at most once.
key_idea: Count magazine letters, then decrement per note letter; any count going negative means a shortage.
approach: Count each letter in magazine
For each letter in ransomNote, decrement its count
Return false if a count drops below zero
Return true after the loop
gotcha: Checking membership only (set) ignores multiplicity; you must track counts.

trigger: Remove exactly k characters to minimize the resulting number or string.
key_idea: A smaller digit should replace any larger digit before it, so maintain a non-decreasing stack and pop while k removals remain.
approach: For each digit, while k > 0 and stack top > digit, pop and decrement k
Push the digit
If k still > 0, chop the last k digits
Strip leading zeros; return '0' if empty
gotcha: Leftover k after the loop (e.g. digits already increasing) must remove from the end, and results like '0200' need leading zeros stripped.

trigger: Longest palindrome you can BUILD from given letters (not find within a string).
key_idea: Every pair of a letter can flank the center; sum all even parts of counts and add one if any letter has an odd count for the middle.
approach: Count each character
For each count add count if even, else count - 1 and flag odd
Add 1 to total if any odd count existed
gotcha: Only ONE odd character can sit in the center; add 1 once, not once per odd count.

trigger: Split a set into two groups with equal sums, which is really 'does some subset sum to total/2'.
key_idea: 0/1 knapsack on reachable sums: for each number, every previously reachable sum plus the number is also reachable.
approach: If total is odd return false; target = total // 2
Start with reachable = {0}
For each num, add num + s for every s in reachable
Return true if target becomes reachable
Return false after processing all numbers
gotcha: With a 1-D boolean array iterate sums from high to low so each number is used at most once.

trigger: Cells that can reach two different borders of a grid under a height rule.
key_idea: Flip the direction: flood from each ocean's border inward, moving only to cells with height >= current, then intersect the two reachable sets.
approach: Create visited sets pacific and atlantic
DFS from top row and left column into pacific set
DFS from bottom row and right column into atlantic set
In DFS move to neighbors with height >= current that are unvisited
Return cells present in both sets
gotcha: Since you traverse in reverse, the neighbor must be HIGHER or equal, not lower; DFS from each cell forward is O((mn)^2).

trigger: Longest substring achievable with at most k changes to make all characters identical.
key_idea: A window is valid when window length minus its most frequent count is <= k; maxFreq never needs to decrease because the answer can only grow with a bigger maxFreq.
approach: Track char counts, left pointer, and max frequency seen
Add s[r] and update max_freq
If (r - l + 1) - max_freq > k, remove s[l] and advance l
Update answer with the window length
gotcha: Not recomputing max_freq on shrink is correct (the window never needs to shrink below the best), which confuses many people.

trigger: Group tree nodes by depth, for a tree where nodes have any number of children.
key_idea: BFS one level at a time; collect the current level's values and gather all children as the next level.
approach: Return [] if root is None
Start queue with the level [root]
For each level, record values and extend next level with node.children
Append the next level to the queue if non-empty
gotcha: children may be None on leaf nodes in some inputs; guard with 'or []' before extending.

trigger: Count downward paths in a tree with a given sum that may start and end anywhere.
key_idea: Subarray-sum-equals-k applied along root-to-node paths: a prefix map of sums on the current path counts ancestors where currSum - target was seen.
approach: prefix_map[0] = 1 for paths starting at the root
DFS with running sum; add node value
Add prefix_map[curr_sum - target] to the answer
Increment prefix_map[curr_sum], recurse both children
Decrement prefix_map[curr_sum] when backtracking
gotcha: Forgetting to undo the prefix count after recursion lets sibling subtrees see each other's ancestors and overcount.

trigger: Find every substring that is a permutation of a pattern string.
key_idea: A fixed-size window of len(p) with matching character counts is an anagram; slide by adding the right char and removing the left one.
approach: Count characters of p
For each r add s[r] to window counts
While s[r] is not in p or its count exceeds p's count, shrink from left
If window counts equal p counts, record l
gotcha: Comparing whole dicts each step is fine for 26 letters but you must delete zero-count keys or the equality check fails.

trigger: Values in range [1, n], O(n) time, and O(1) extra space: the array itself is your hash map.
key_idea: Cyclic sort places value v at index v - 1; afterwards any index holding the wrong value holds a duplicate. Alternatively negate nums[abs(v) - 1] as a visited mark.
approach: i = 0; while i < n, let j = nums[i] - 1
If nums[j] != nums[i], swap them (do not advance i)
Else advance i
Collect nums[i] wherever nums[i] != i + 1
gotcha: Only advance i when the element is in place or a duplicate blocks it; comparing values (not indices) avoids infinite swap loops on duplicates.

trigger: Check whether a set of partial orderings determines exactly one full ordering that matches a given sequence.
key_idea: Kahn's algorithm yields a unique topological order only if the queue never holds more than one node; verify that order equals nums.
approach: Set in-degree 0 for every number in nums
For each consecutive pair in each sequence, add edge and bump in-degree
Queue nodes with in-degree 0
If queue ever has more than one node, return false
Pop and compare to nums at that position; return false on mismatch
Return true only if all nums were produced
gotcha: A queue size above 1 means two valid orderings exist; also return false if the result is shorter than nums (cycle).

trigger: Values in range [1, n] with some missing; the O(1)-space follow-up hints at index marking.
key_idea: Use indices as a bitmap: mark index v - 1 (negate or cyclic-sort into place) for every value; unmarked indices are missing. The learner's set version is simpler but O(n) space.
approach: For each value v, negate nums[abs(v) - 1] if positive
Scan indices; i + 1 is missing wherever nums[i] is positive
Return the collected numbers
gotcha: Use abs(v) when indexing because earlier iterations may have already negated that value.

trigger: Exactly one number from [0, n] is absent from an array of n distinct values.
key_idea: Expected sum n(n+1)/2 minus the actual sum is the missing number; XOR of all indices and values cancels everything except it.
approach: Compute expected = n * (n + 1) // 2
Subtract sum(nums)
Return the difference
gotcha: The range is [0, n] so the missing value can be n itself; a loop over 0..n-1 must fall through to return n.

trigger: Reorder characters so the most frequent come first.
key_idea: Count, then bucket by frequency (max is len(s)) and emit from highest bucket down, repeating each char count times.
approach: Count characters
Create len(s) + 1 buckets; put each char in bucket[freq]
Walk buckets from high to low
Append char * freq for each char
gotcha: Repeated string concatenation in a loop can be slow; build a list and join.

trigger: Find indices i < j < k with nums[i] < nums[k] < nums[j], a 'peak in the middle' subsequence.
key_idea: Push each number with the minimum seen before it; a decreasing stack lets you check whether some earlier peak with a smaller pre-minimum brackets the current value.
approach: Track running minimum min_v
Pop stack entries whose value <= current number
If top value > current and top's min < current, return true
Push (current, min_v)
gotcha: Update min_v before pushing but the pair must use the min BEFORE the pushed element; the alternative right-to-left scan tracking 'third' is equally common.

trigger: Following jumps in an array and asking whether they form a cycle (of length > 1, single direction).
key_idea: Each index is a linked-list node whose next is (i + nums[i]) mod n; run Floyd's cycle detection from each start, bailing out if direction changes or a self-loop appears.
approach: For each start i, set slow = fast = i and record direction
nextIndex returns -1 if direction flips or it points to itself
Advance slow once and fast twice until -1 or they meet
If they met (not -1), return true
Return false after all starts

complexity.time: O(n) with marking visited, O(n^2) naive

gotcha: A cycle of length 1 (element jumping to itself) does not count, and mixing forward and backward moves invalidates the path.

trigger: Count the ways to assign + or - to each number to hit a target.
key_idea: State is (index, running total); memoizing it turns the 2^n decision tree into O(n * sumRange). Equivalently, count subsets summing to (total + target) / 2.
approach: Define dfs(i, total): at i == n return 1 if total == target
Return memo if (i, total) already computed
Recurse with total + nums[i] and total - nums[i]
Store and return the sum of both branches
gotcha: Without memoization it is exponential; totals can be negative so use a dict (or offset) rather than a plain array.

trigger: For each element find the first larger element to its right.
key_idea: Scan nums2 with a decreasing stack; when a larger number arrives it is the next greater for every smaller value popped, recorded in a map.
approach: For each n in nums2, pop stack while top < n and map popped -> n
Push n
Answer each nums1 value with map.get(value, -1)
gotcha: Elements still on the stack at the end have no greater element, so the map lookup must default to -1.

trigger: A value defined by a recurrence on the previous one or two values.
key_idea: Overlapping subproblems: memoize F(n) top-down, or iterate with two rolling variables.
approach: Base cases F(0) = 0, F(1) = 1
Iterate from 2 to n keeping prev and curr
curr, prev = curr + prev, curr
Return curr
gotcha: Naive recursion without memo is O(2^n); iterative version also avoids recursion depth limits.

trigger: Per-level aggregate (max, sum, average) over a binary tree.
key_idea: Level-order traversal; for each level compute the maximum before moving to the children.
approach: Return [] if root is None
Queue the root as the first level
For each level track max value and collect non-null children
Append the max; enqueue next level if non-empty
gotcha: Initialize the level max with -infinity, since node values can be negative.

trigger: Longest palindromic SUBSEQUENCE (deletions allowed), which is an interval DP on (l, r).
key_idea: If s[l] == s[r] they wrap a smaller palindrome (2 + dp(l+1, r-1)); otherwise drop one end and take the better of the two.
approach: Memoized dfs(l, r): return 0 if l > r, 1 if l == r
If s[l] == s[r], result = dfs(l+1, r-1) + 2
Else result = max(dfs(l+1, r), dfs(l, r-1))
Store and return; answer is dfs(0, n-1)
gotcha: The l == r base case returns 1, and equals LCS of s with its reverse; recursion depth can hit limits for n near 1000.

trigger: Longest path between any two nodes in a tree, not necessarily through the root.
key_idea: Post-order DFS returns each subtree's height; at every node the candidate diameter is left height + right height, tracked in an outer variable.
approach: dfs(node) returns 0 for None
Compute left and right heights recursively
Update diameter = max(diameter, left + right)
Return max(left, right) + 1
gotcha: Returning the diameter instead of the height from the recursion breaks the parent's calculation; diameter counts edges, not nodes.

trigger: Count connected components given an adjacency matrix.
key_idea: Start with n components and each successful union merges two, so components = n minus successful unions. DFS marking visited works equally well.
approach: Create union-find with parent and rank arrays
For every isConnected[i][j] == 1, union(i, j)
Subtract 1 from the count for each union that merged distinct roots
Return the count
gotcha: Union must return whether it merged (roots differed); without path compression find degrades to O(n).

trigger: Count contiguous subarrays with an exact sum, possibly with negative numbers.
key_idea: Subarray sum = prefix[r] - prefix[l]; count how many earlier prefixes equal current - k using a frequency map.
approach: freq[0] = 1 for subarrays starting at index 0
Keep a running total
Add freq[total - k] to the answer
Increment freq[total]
gotcha: Seeding freq[0] = 1 and adding to the answer BEFORE recording the current prefix are both required.

trigger: Pair up elements to maximize the sum of the minimum of each pair.
key_idea: Sorting and pairing neighbors wastes the least: each large number is 'sacrificed' next to the nearest smaller one.
approach: Sort the array
Sum every element at even index
Return the sum
gotcha: Pairing smallest with largest feels intuitive but is wrong; adjacent pairing is optimal.

trigger: Does a string contain any permutation of another string as a substring.
key_idea: Same as find-all-anagrams: a window of len(s1) with identical char counts is a permutation; slide and compare counts.
approach: Count characters of s1
For each r add s2[r] to window counts
While s2[r] is not in s1 or its count exceeds s1's, shrink from left
If window counts equal s1 counts, return true
Return false
gotcha: Delete zero-count keys before comparing dicts, or track a 'matches' counter over 26 letters to keep comparison O(1).

trigger: Check whether one tree appears exactly, structure and values, somewhere inside another.
key_idea: At each node of root, test isSameTree with subRoot; otherwise recurse into left and right children.
approach: If subRoot is None return true; if root is None return false
If isSameTree(root, subRoot) return true
Return isSubtree(root.left) or isSubtree(root.right)
isSameTree compares values and recurses on both children
gotcha: isSameTree must require both subtrees to end at the same time (both None), otherwise a partial match is accepted.
